29th. October, 1931.

Sir,

I have the honour to acknowledge and
thank you for your letter of October 27th. on
the subject of the Thorburn case. I note that
the source of your information is to be kept
entirely confidential.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

Consul-General.

R.C. Aiers, Esquire,
Deputy Commissioner,
(Crime Branch),
Shanghai Municipal Police,
Shanghai.

1931 年 10 月 29 日。

先生：

谨此确认收到您 10 月 27 日关于索伯恩（Thorburn）一案的来信，并致谢意。我知悉，您的信息来源须予以严格保密。

谨此致意，
先生，
您顺从的仆人，

总领事。

R.C. Aiers 先生，
副巡官，
（刑事股），
上海公共租界工部局警务处，
上海。

page_data.en:
CONFIDENTIAL.

October 27, 31.

Sir,

Thorburn Case.

I have the honour to forward the following
information received by me. I cannot vouch that it
is correct, but it has been forwarded through a source
which is usually reliable and comes from Nanking:
"Thorburn was murdered in a shocking way (details
unknown to informer or if known he will not divulge)
about the 4th day after his arrival at Soochow. His
body was conveyed to Sz Sz San ( Lion Hill ) (獅子山)
near Soochow where it was burnt on the instructions of
a Captain of Military Police named Wong Ching Ziang.
黄 振 祥
This Captain is said to be a man about 30 years of age
and was formerly a cadet in the Whangpoa Military College,
Canton. It is reported that he was arrested and sentenced
to 3 years imprisonment by Military Court in Nanking for
Breach of Military discipline in connection with this
murder and is at present in gaol there, where he has
made a complete confession."

If you consider this of any value and desire
to use it to make enquiries, I shall be glad if you

机密。

1931 年 10 月 27 日。

先生：

索伯恩案。

谨呈上我所收到的下列情报。我无法保证该情报确凿无误，但其经由通常可靠的渠道转来，源自南京：
“索伯恩在抵达苏州后约第四天，以令人震惊的方式被谋杀（详情为线人所不知，或即便知晓亦不愿透露）。其遗体被运至苏州附近的 Sz Sz San（狮子山）(獅子山)，并根据一名名为黄振祥（Wong Ching Ziang）的宪兵队长的指令予以焚毁。
黄 振 祥
据称，该队长年约三十岁，曾是广州黄埔军校的学生。据报道，他因涉及此谋杀案违反军纪，被南京军事法庭逮捕并判处三年监禁，目前正囚禁于该处，并已作出完全供认。”

will keep the source of information confidential
as I am bound to secrecy in the matter, and the
knowledge that this office is the transmitting
agency would probably cause serious consequences
both for my informer and the man concerned, who
holds an official position in Nanking.

It was also said that official pressure
at the present time would probably bring results
if the above was questioned.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your Obedient Servant,

Deputy Commissioner
(Crime Branch)

H.B.M. Consul-General,
Shanghai.

对信息来源予以保密，我将不胜感激，因为我对此事负有保密义务；且若得知本办事处为传递机构，可能会给提供情报者以及那位在南京担任公职的相关人士带来严重后果。

另据悉，若就上述情况进行质询，目前施加官方压力可能会取得成效。

谨此致意，
先生，
您顺从的仆人，

副巡官
（刑事股）

英国驻上海总领事，
上海。
